variants.label: Base café
variants.subtitle: Single storey · striped awning
variants.difference: The shared starting point: a flat roof, three-bay storefront and striped awning.

variants.label: Upstairs café
variants.subtitle: Same footprint · upper floor
variants.difference: The base café with one upper floor. Ground-floor proportions, entry and furniture stay the same.

variants.label: Compact café
variants.subtitle: Narrower frontage · upper floor
variants.difference: A narrower frontage and shallower footprint, using the same storefront, windows and awning modules.

variants.label: Blue-awning unit
variants.subtitle: Solid blue awning · vacant
variants.difference: The same upstairs shell with a solid-blue awning and an empty interior, preserving Sid’s candidate unit.

variants.label: Corner café
variants.subtitle: Wider footprint · corner glazing
variants.difference: A wider base with glazing around the corner, rooftop enclosure and an extra seating set.

variants.label: Base office
variants.subtitle: Four storeys · paired side windows
variants.difference: The shared base: ribbon windows on the street façade, paired windows on the sides, a glazed entrance and a small rooftop enclosure.

variants.label: Wide office
variants.subtitle: Broader footprint · continuous bands
variants.difference: A wider, deeper and slightly taller version with continuous window bands, an offset entrance, and a larger rooftop enclosure with a vent.

variants.label: Low office wing
variants.subtitle: Three storeys · compact footprint
variants.difference: The lower rear wing uses the same window bays and parapet. Its visible street façade keeps uninterrupted bands. An entrance on the obscured side and the other hidden details are inferred from the shared system.

variants.label: Base small home
variants.subtitle: One storey · flat parapet roof
variants.difference: The shared starting point: a low rectangular shell, framed windows, a single door and a flat parapet roof. The entrance sits in the area obscured by the reference tree.

variants.label: Gatehouse
variants.subtitle: Service glazing · striped awning
variants.difference: The same shell with a glazed service face, counter ledge and the café family’s shared striped awning. The unseen rear access uses the standard single door.

variants.label: Utility hut
variants.subtitle: Minimal shell · plain flat roof
variants.difference: The smallest shell: a plain roof and one visible paired window. A short rear access door is inferred using the shared door system.

variants.label: Compact home
variants.subtitle: Stacked side windows · plain roof
variants.referenceLabel: Compact building west of the towers
variants.difference: A taller compact configuration with the reference’s two rows of small side windows and a double entrance. The drawing does not establish an internal floor plan.

variants.label: Compact store
variants.subtitle: Double service doors · parapet roof
variants.difference: A compact storage or utility configuration with double service doors. The partly hidden side stays simple; dimensions and openings are declared rather than scaled per instance.

variants.label: Frontage unit
variants.subtitle: Glazed double entry · side window
variants.referenceLabel: Small unit along the society frontage
variants.difference: The compact shell with a warm glazed double entrance and paired side window, matching the small frontage building. No café signage or furniture is added.

variants.label: Utility block
variants.subtitle: Wider shell · two glazed door sets
variants.difference: A wider configuration of the same shell, with two separate glazed door sets and two side windows. Its utility use is an interpretation of the unlabeled reference.

variants.label: Home + annex
variants.subtitle: Rooftop box · attached utility shell
variants.difference: The larger home adds a rooftop enclosure and an attached, smaller version of the utility shell. The annex has its own source ID and a shared internal connection; hidden access details are inferred.

masters.label: Scooter
masters.referenceLabel: Parked scooter in the lower-right parking bays
masters.description: A compact step-through body, rounded leg shield, short saddle and small matching wheels. Mirrors, lamps and a center stand complete the parked master.

masters.label: Bicycle
masters.referenceLabel: Bicycle beside the central parking area
masters.description: An open diamond frame with two matching spoked wheels, fork, saddle, swept handlebars, pedals and a simple chain drive. A kickstand supports the parked master.

poses.label: Standing
poses.subtitle: Relaxed, balanced stance
poses.referenceLabel: Standing figure beside the central parking
poses.description: The base person: rounded head, simple shirt, relaxed arms and two grounded feet.

poses.label: Walking
poses.subtitle: A static mid-stride pose
poses.referenceLabel: Walking figure on the central pavement
poses.description: The same proportions with a clear stride, opposite arm swing and a slight forward lean. This is a static pose.

poses.label: Seated
poses.subtitle: Fitted to the approved café chair
poses.referenceLabel: Seated café guest in the foreground row
poses.description: Hips meet the café seat, both feet meet the ground, and relaxed hands rest above the thighs. The chair is a separate approved component.

poses.label: Riding · scooter
poses.subtitle: Seat, grips & floorboard contact
poses.referenceLabel: Scooter rider on the southern road
poses.description: A forward lean brings both hands to the grips. Hips rest on the saddle and feet sit on the floorboard. The scooter keeps its approved dimensions.

poses.label: Riding · bicycle
poses.subtitle: Seat, grips & pedal contact
poses.referenceLabel: Person beside the lower-right bicycle; riding fit inferred
poses.description: The same body leans farther forward to reach the bicycle’s grips. Feet meet the opposing pedals and hips meet the saddle. This fitted pose interprets the reference’s simplified people.

masters.label: Lamp
masters.subtitle: Lantern head · stepped base
masters.description: A slim pole with a stepped foot, tapered glazed lantern and shallow pyramidal cap. One unchanged master for every lamp.

masters.label: Bollard
masters.subtitle: Rounded cap · circular foot
masters.description: A short slender post, rounded cap and compact circular base. The pale shaft and cobalt contour echo the small repeated pavement posts.

masters.label: Bench
masters.subtitle: Five slats · open seat
masters.description: A low backless bench with five real seat slats, two under-seat supports and four connected feet. The open construction follows the courtyard reference.

masters.label: Bin
masters.subtitle: Inferred · recessed opening
masters.description: A simple cylindrical bin with a recessed top opening, thin rim and removable lid seam. This is an inferred kit component: the reference does not show a clearly identifiable bin.

masters.label: Fence panel
masters.subtitle: 13 pickets · shared end anchors
masters.description: A repeatable panel with thirteen pickets, top and bottom rails, and fixed end anchors. The fence assembly preview connects three copies to four gateposts.

masters.label: Gatepost
masters.subtitle: Square pier · inset plaque
masters.description: A square pier with a thin cap, pale inset plaque and two pairs of panel attachment points. The same post closes every panel joint.

referenceNotes.bin: No unambiguous source bin is visible. The requested bin master is an inferred kit component, with no invented source instance.
referenceNotes.bounds: Small pole caps and occluded bases use provisional review boxes; verify these boundaries during composition review.
referenceNotes.fence: Three visible housing fence runs map to the same panel. Whole-panel repeat counts remain unassigned; no per-instance scaling.
referenceNotes.excluded: The metro canopy, stair rails and perimeter railing remain part of the separate metro checkpoint.

parts.label: Stairs & landings
parts.subtitle: Eight steps · two landings
parts.description: Eight repeated treads connect the covered upper landing to the lower landing. The ground anchor stays at the upper entrance; the well extends below it.

parts.label: Perimeter railing
parts.subtitle: Posts · pickets · open approach
parts.description: Shared vertical posts and pickets enclose the open well. The full-width approach under the canopy stays clear.

parts.label: Stair handrails
parts.subtitle: Two continuous rails
parts.description: Two continuous rails follow the stair pitch, with short level returns at each landing. Supports connect to the stair side walls.

parts.label: Canopy & glazing
parts.subtitle: Shared frame · clear panes
parts.description: Four slim columns support a shallow rectangular frame and six transparent roof panes. Side glazing leaves the entrance open.

parts.label: Metro sign
parts.subtitle: A geometric M on both faces
parts.description: A cobalt circular sign carries a geometric white M on both faces. Its mast shares the canopy corner.

metro.inference: Stair depth, tread count and concealed structure are coherent interpretations of the single reference.

variants.label: Straight road
variants.subtitle: Pale-blue surface
variants.description: A quiet pale-blue road surface, with a shared width and connection anchors at both ends. Markings are separate reusable parts.

variants.label: Road junction
variants.subtitle: Four matching connections
variants.description: One continuous four-way surface. Its arms meet the same straight-road width without overlapping asphalt planes.

variants.label: Tiled pavement
variants.subtitle: Shared grid · subtle seams
variants.description: White paving uses a restrained square grid, a shallow raised edge and the same grade as the approved building and furniture anchors.

variants.label: Rounded plaza
variants.subtitle: Open paving · softened corners
variants.description: A square plaza with rounded corners and the same paving system. Its open surface leaves space for the later furniture and people placements.

variants.label: Lowered crossing edge
variants.subtitle: Flush connection to the road
variants.description: A shallow, flared section lowers the pavement to road height at a crossing. Its grid follows the real sloping surface. The concealed slope is an inferred connection detail.

variants.label: Kerb segment
variants.subtitle: Repeatable edge profile
variants.description: One short kerb with a lightly bevelled edge. End anchors allow repeated runs; the pavement pieces use the same height and pale edge treatment.

variants.label: Zebra crossing
variants.subtitle: Eight shared white bars
variants.description: Eight equal white bars read clearly on the pale road. The set stays within the carriageway and aligns with the lowered pavement approach.

variants.label: Lane dash
variants.subtitle: One repeatable marking
variants.description: A short white dash repeats along the road center. The crossing fit keeps the centerline out of the pedestrian crossing.

variants.label: Parking bay
variants.subtitle: Open-ended white outline
variants.description: One U-shaped bay marking repeats at a fixed pitch. The parking preview shows four bays, with clear entry edges and a shared back line.

variants.label: Circular courtyard
variants.subtitle: Pale inset · white rim
variants.description: A low white rim surrounds a pale-blue circular inset, following the housing courtyard reference. Its use is left unspecified; there is no invented fountain or planting.

variants.label: Metro pavement
variants.subtitle: Real opening for the stairwell
variants.description: The paving is cut around the approved metro stairwell. Grid lines stop at the opening, while the upper landing joins the pavement at the same height.
